pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis secondary to an Ovarian Teratoma THE SMOKING GUN: The presence of an EEG showing an extreme delta brush pattern alongside a pelvic teratoma in a young female with acute onset psychosis, dyskinesias, and autonomic dysfunction. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: The patient possessed an unsuspected mature ovarian teratoma containing nervous tissue. The immune system recognized this ectopic neural tissue as foreign, mounting an immune response against the GluN1 subunit of NMDA receptors. These circulating autoantibodies cross-reacted with central nervous system NMDA receptors, causing antibody-mediated receptor cross-linking and internalization. The resulting depletion of synaptic NMDA receptors disrupted frontostriatal pathways, triggering acute psychiatric symptoms, involuntary movements, severe autonomic dysfunction, and central hypoventilation. Treatment requires surgical excision of the teratoma and high-dose immunotherapy.
